Feature: Case-insensitive whitespace tokenisation
User story: As an admin, I want my query split into words regardless of case and extra spaces so that 'GET  mguser' and 'get mguser' find the same cmdlets.
Expected behaviour: queryTokens (sources.ts) lower-cases the query, splits it on any run of whitespace and keeps only pieces that contain a letter or digit. A piece made only of hyphens or punctuation ('--', '-') is not a token. Names are compared against lower-cased copies (search-core.ts prepareSource, searchHits). Leading, trailing and repeated spaces add no tokens. A query with zero tokens (blank, whitespace-only or hyphen-only) is no query at all. Every row is listed in index order, with no highlight. The count label shows no '· N ms' timing, because Search (App.tsx) tests queryTokens of results.q, not the raw string. The query reaches the URL trimmed: writeUrl writes q.trim() and leaves q out when that is blank, and readUrl trims a pasted q. The box keeps what was typed until a reload. The same tokeniser drives result-name highlighting (ResultList.tsx Mark). locate finds each token literally, or else ignoring hyphens on both sides through flatMatch, and maps the hit back to the name's own characters. Overlapping marks are sorted by start, and at the same start the longer one wins, so 'get get-mguser' highlights the whole 'Get-MgUser'. A token matched only by the typo fallback (SRCH-07) gets no <mark>.
How to test: 1) Open / and wait for the results. Type 'GET-MGUSER', then replace it with '  get-mguser  '. Both give '573 results' in the same order, the first row is Get-MgUser with the whole name in a <mark>, and the URL reads /?q=get-mguser with no padding. Reload: the box shows 'get-mguser'. 2) Search 'get get-mguser'. On the first row, Get-MgUser, the whole name 'Get-MgUser' is in a single <mark>, not just 'Get'. 3) Clear the box and type three spaces. The count reads '40,931 results' with no '· N ms', the URL stays '/' (no q parameter), and the first row is Add-MgApplicationKey, as with an empty box. 4) Search '--', then '-'. Each gives '40,931 results' with no timing, rows in index order (first row Add-MgApplicationKey) and no <mark> on any row.
Code refs: src/app/sources.ts (queryTokens, flatMatch); src/app/search-core.ts (prepareSource, searchHits); src/app/ResultList.tsx (locate, Mark); src/app/App.tsx (Search); src/app/url.ts (readUrl, writeUrl)

Feature: Typo-tolerant fuzzy matching
User story: As an admin, I want slightly misspelled queries to still find cmdlets so that a typo mid-task does not return nothing.
Expected behaviour: Typo tolerance is an edit-distance fallback for a token that occurs literally nowhere in scope. Literally means as a name, prefix, noun-prefix, substring or flat match, or in a loaded description, counting only rows that pass the filters. searchHits (search-core.ts) marks such a token misspelt for the whole search and typo-scores it for every row (typoScore). typoBudget allows 0 edits below 5 letters, 1 edit for 5-10 letters and 2 beyond. prefixDistance counts insertions, deletions, substitutions and swaps of adjacent letters, a swap counting as one edit. It measures the distance from the token to the closest prefix of several strings: the hyphen-free name, the whole name, and the name from every word start of the noun (after the verb's hyphen and at each camel-case capital, from wordStarts). So 'licnese' matches the License in Set-MgUserLicense. A cheap prefilter rejects a candidate before the table is built unless one of the token's first max+1 letters appears in its first 2*max+1 characters. Within budget, the score is 300 - 100*edits - min(60, nameLength - tokenLength): about 140-200 for one edit and 40-100 for two (a name shorter than the token adds the difference back). Typo matches never mix with literal matches of the same token, so they cannot crowd out real hits. A typo-matched token is not highlighted. The client keeps at most one search with the worker (SRCH-16), so a slow typo scan never builds a backlog while the user types.
How to test: 1) Search 'get-mgsuer' (swapped letters). Get-MgUser is the first row, followed by other Get-MgUser* names (681 results), and no row has a <mark>. 2) Search 'get-mgusr' (dropped letter). Get-MgUser is the first row. 3) Search 'licnese' (98 results). Set-MgUserLicense is the first row, and Set-MgGroupLicense and other *License names follow, unhighlighted. Search 'mguser licnese' (6 results). Set-MgUserLicense comes first, then Get-MgUserLicenseDetail and the other *MgUserLicenseDetail* names. 4) Search 'get-mguser'. The 573 results are all literal matches, with no typo rows mixed in. 5) Search 'xyzq'. It is 4 letters, so it has no typo budget, and the result is '0 results' with the 'No match for “xyzq”.' empty state. 6) Focus the box and type 'set-mgusrlicensedetial' as fast as possible. The count and list show the final query's result within about a second of the last keystroke, not after seconds of stale updates.

Each source's state goes from 'loading' to 'ready', or to 'failed' if the fetch fails ('[psindex] descriptions failed' is logged and setDescriptions in search-core.ts receives null). That source then keeps name-only search. When every fetch has settled, the worker re-runs the latest search under the same id, so the client still accepts it, and description matches and text are added. When they are 'failed', a notice above the results reads 'Descriptions didn’t load, so only cmdlet names are searched.' with a Reload button (chrome.tsx DescriptionsFailed). An empty result then shows the final 'No match for “<q>”.' state, which is not busy. While no results have arrived, the count reads 'Loading index…' (App.tsx Search).

Expected behaviour: With focus in the search box, ArrowDown/ArrowUp move the cursor by one row (default prevented so the caret does not move), clamped to the first and last rows; with no results, or no list mounted (load error), they do nothing. The list scrolls just enough to keep the cursor row visible (minimal scroll, top or bottom aligned). The search box is a combobox (role=combobox, aria-controls=results) whose aria-activedescendant names the cursor row's id (result-<i>) while that row is rendered; the cursor row has aria-selected=true. A new search (new results id) resets the cursor to the first row and scrolls to the top; a refresh of the same search (descriptions arriving) keeps the cursor on the same row (following it if reordered, falling back to the first row if it is gone) and reveals it.

Search 'qqqzzz' (no results) and press ArrowDown: nothing changes.

Feature: Enter opens the cursor row, including before results arrive
User story: As an admin, I want to type a name and press Enter immediately so that the top match opens even if the search hasn't finished.
Expected behaviour: Enter in the search box (default prevented) records a pending selection for the latest search id (client.latest) while keeping the currently open entry shown. When that search's results are on screen, the cursor row is opened (fetched from the worker if not yet materialised). If those results are empty the pending Enter is dropped and the previously shown entry remains. Typing again or changing filters before results arrive gives up the pending Enter (settle) and keeps what was shown; clicking another row also supersedes it. Escape while an Enter is pending gives up only that Enter: the query stays as typed and the pane keeps what it showed (a further Escape then closes the entry or clears the query, see LIST-09). Enter replaces a deep-link lookup still in progress. Enter with no list mounted (load error) does nothing. Before hydration the server-rendered search box is read-only, so nothing typed is accepted and then lost; once the session mounts, the live box takes focus and accepts typing while the index is still loading.

Feature: Escape closes the entry, then clears the query
User story: As an admin, I want Escape to back out step by step so that I can quickly reset without the mouse.
Expected behaviour: Escape is handled globally (anywhere on the page except inside a select) and its default is prevented, so the search input does not also clear itself natively. It backs out one step, the first that applies: a pending Enter (LIST-08) is given up, keeping the query and whatever the pane showed; else, if an entry is open (or a deep link is still being looked up), the entry closes at once and focus returns to the search box, keeping the query; else, if the query is non-empty, it is cleared. With nothing pending or open and an empty query it does nothing. On narrow screens the open entry is a history entry of its own: closing it with Escape also drops that entry with a single history.back() (guarded, so a repeated Escape fired before popstate pops it only once and never leaves the page), and the full-screen detail pane slides away.
How to test: Search 'user', press Enter to open the first row, press Escape: the detail closes (Intro visible, `.app` has no data-open, URL loses c= but keeps q=user), the search box value is still 'user' and document.activeElement is the search input. Press Escape again: the value is '', q is gone from the URL and the clear button is replaced by the '/' hint. Open a row, click inside the detail pane text, press Escape: the entry closes and focus returns to the search box. At 390x844, search 'user', tap the first row and press Escape: the overlay slides away, the value is 'user', and the page is still PSIndex (location.pathname '/', q=user). At 390x844 with a marked history entry behind the page (history.replaceState({marker:'seed'}), then pushState({marker:'page'})), search 'get-mguser', press Enter, then dispatch two Escape keydowns on document.body in the same tick: exactly one popstate fires, history.state.marker is 'page', the detail is closed and the value is still 'get-mguser'.

Feature: Narrow dialog history: one Back per close, and widening drops the entry
User story: As a phone user, I want closing a cmdlet to undo exactly one history step, and a rotated or widened window not to leave a stray entry, so that I never fall off PSIndex or close the wrong thing with Back.
Expected behaviour: The narrow-screen (<=900px) entry dialog pushes one history entry when it opens (NAV-16). In-app closes (Escape, 'Back to results', the wordmark, Dismiss) go through dropEntry. It calls history.back() at most once while a drop is in flight (the dropping ref) and closes the entry immediately, without waiting for popstate. A key-repeated Escape, or a double click on Back that fires before popstate, therefore pops exactly one entry and stays on the page with the query kept. The popstate a drop causes is recognised as ours: it does not close anything again, and it rewrites the current URL (writeUrl), because history.back() restored the URL from before the dialog. If the window widens past 900px while an entry is open, the dialog ends (no role=dialog, no inert), and the leftover entry is popped. The entry stays open, and c= stays in the URL. A later browser Back then leaves for the previous page instead of closing the cmdlet. If the layout is narrow again when the drop's popstate lands, the entry is pushed again, so Back still closes the dialog. A browser or phone Back that the app did not start closes the entry as before.
How to test: Serve the build locally (`node tests/e2e.cjs` covers it as 'dialog history stays on the page'). By hand with Playwright at 390x844: 1) Load /?q=seed-marker and wait for rows. Call setViewportSize(1200x800). __pops goes up by 1, .pane-detail has no role=dialog, the title is still Get-MgUser and c=graph:Get-MgUser stays in the URL. 5) Call page.goBack(): history.state.marker becomes 'seed' and q=seed-marker. Back went to the previous page, not just closing the cmdlet. 6) Double-click 'Back to results' at 390x844: same result as step 3.
Code refs: src/app/App.tsx (useNarrow, Search); src/app/url.ts (writeUrl); tests/e2e.cjs (scenarios)

Feature: Worker runs only the latest search after the index loads
User story: As an admin typing quickly while the index is still loading, I want only my final query to be computed so that the first results show up as soon as possible.
Expected behaviour: SearchClient keeps at most one search with the worker. Each search() call makes its query the latest search and stores it as the one waiting search, replacing any earlier waiting one. The search is posted at once only when no search is running. When the results for the running search arrive, the waiting search, if any, is posted, so searches typed while another is with the worker are never sent unless they are still the latest. The page receives only results whose id is the latest search's. The worker records each search it receives as lastSearch and runs it once the index promise resolves. Once descriptions load, it re-runs lastSearch under the same id, so that search gets a second results message. While the index is loading, the mount's first search (q '') is the one with the worker, and only the last query typed waits. Intermediate queries never reach the worker. Requests (rows, related, find) are not coalesced and are answered in arrival order once the index loads.

Assert the first .result-name contains 'Get'.

Only then is .staging renamed to public/a/<build> (or dropped if that build already exists), the other entries in public/a/ are removed, and src/sources.generated.json is written as {build, total, sources:[{id,label,short,color,sample,extra,count,version}]}. Feature: Per-source refresh with atomic swap (refresh.sh)
User story: As a maintainer, I want to refresh one source at a time into a temp directory and only replace data/<source>/ when its parser succeeds so that a failed run leaves committed data untouched and upstream deletions are reflected.
Expected behaviour: `bash pipelines/refresh.sh <id>` exits 1 with 'usage: pipelines/refresh.sh <source>' when the argument is missing. It sources pipelines/<id>/source.env for REPO, SPARSE and PARSE_DIR and clones into a mktemp directory: shallow --depth 1, or with a non-empty SPARSE, --filter=blob:none --sparse plus `sparse-checkout set SPARSE`. exchange has SPARSE=(), so it gets a full shallow clone; az uses --no-cone 'azps-*/Az.*'. It then runs parse_docs.py with PSINDEX_OUT=<tmp>/out and PYTHONPATH=pipelines on <docs>/<PARSE_DIR>. Under set -euo pipefail, any failure exits before `rm -rf data/<id>`. Feature: Streamable HTTP endpoint at /mcp: initialize, JSON responses and request checks
User story: As an agent developer, I want PSIndex to answer the Model Context Protocol at /mcp so that Cursor, Claude or VS Code can use the cmdlet index with only a URL in their config.
Expected behaviour: src/pages/mcp.ts is the only non-prerendered route (prerender = false). GET, POST, DELETE and OPTIONS all go to handleMcp. A POST carries a JSON-RPC message. 'initialize' answers HTTP 200, content-type application/json (enableJsonResponse: plain JSON, not an SSE stream), with result.serverInfo {name 'psindex', version '1.0.0'}, result.capabilities.tools, the protocolVersion the client asked for (e.g. '2025-03-26') and result.instructions 'Search and read Microsoft 365 and Azure PowerShell cmdlets from PSIndex. Use search_cmdlets to find a name, then get_cmdlet for its syntax and parameters. Read-only.' The SDK transport enforces the HTTP contract: a POST whose Accept lacks either application/json or text/event-stream gets 406 with JSON-RPC error -32000 'Not Acceptable: Client must accept both application/json and text/event-stream'. A non-JSON content-type gets 415. A body that is not JSON gets 400 with error -32700 'Parse error: Invalid JSON'. A notification (no id, e.g. notifications/initialized) gets 202 with no body. If connecting or handling throws, the reply is 500 with {jsonrpc '2.0', error {code -32603, message 'Internal server error'}, id null}, and the error is logged as '[psindex] mcp'. README.md 'MCP' documents the URL https://psindex.vercel.app/mcp, that it is stateless, read-only and unauthenticated, the three tools, and a {"mcpServers":{"psindex":{"url":...}}} client config.
How to test: 1) `npm run build` with VERCEL unset (Node adapter), then `HOST=127.0.0.1 PORT=4410 node dist/server/entry.mjs` (or `npm run preview -- --port 4410`, which serves the same build). 2) `curl -si -H 'content-type: application/json' -H 'accept: application/json, text/event-stream' http://127.0.0.1:4410/mcp -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2025-03-26","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"t","version":"1"}}}'`: 200, content-type application/json, serverInfo.name 'psindex', version '1.0.0', capabilities.tools present, the instructions text above. 3) Repeat with `-H 'accept: application/json'` only: 406 and 'Client must accept both application/json and text/event-stream'. 4) Send `-H 'content-type: text/plain'`: 415. 5) Send body `{bad`: 400 and code -32700 'Parse error: Invalid JSON'. 6) POST `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"notifications/initialized"}`: 202, empty body. 7) `grep -n -A12 '## MCP' README.md` shows the endpoint URL and the mcpServers JSON.

Feature: Stateless server: no sessions, a fresh server per request
User story: As an agent developer, I want every /mcp request to stand alone so that my client works without session handshakes and the endpoint can run as a stateless serverless function.
Expected behaviour: dispatch builds a new McpServer and a new WebStandardStreamableHTTPServerTransport for every request with sessionIdGenerator undefined, and closes the server in finally. No response carries an mcp-session-id header, and no request needs one: tools/list or tools/call work as the first request with no initialize before them. A GET with Accept: text/event-stream answers 200, content-type text/event-stream, and the stream ends at once, because the server closes after the request (there is no standing notification stream). A GET without that Accept gets 406 'Not Acceptable: Client must accept text/event-stream'. A DELETE (session termination) answers 200 with an empty body, because there is no session to end. Every response sets cache-control: no-store. astro.config.mjs sets session: false, so Astro ships no session store.
How to test: Start the local server as in MCP-01 step 1. 1) Without calling initialize, `curl -si -H 'content-type: application/json' -H 'accept: application/json, text/event-stream' http://127.0.0.1:4410/mcp -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/list"}'`: 200 with the three tools. The headers have no mcp-session-id line (the name appears only inside access-control-allow-headers), and cache-control is no-store. 2) Send the initialize from MCP-01: no mcp-session-id header in the response either. 3) `curl -s -m 10 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} %{time_total}\n' -H 'accept: text/event-stream' http://127.0.0.1:4410/mcp`: 200, returning well under the 10 s timeout. 4) `curl -si http://127.0.0.1:4410/mcp`: 406 with 'Client must accept text/event-stream'. 5) `curl -si -X DELETE http://127.0.0.1:4410/mcp`: 200 and an empty body. 6) `grep -n 'session' astro.config.mjs` shows 'session: false'.

Feature: Index read from disk, cached, with a recoverable failure
User story: As the maintainer, I want the MCP function to read the same build artifacts the page fetches and to recover from a failed read so that MCP answers always match the deployed site, and a transient error does not stick until a cold start.
